ideas.children_he: יַעֲקֹב הֵבִין שֶׁהִגִּיעַ הַזְּמַן לַחֲזֹר הַבַּיְתָה.
ideas.children_en: Jacob heard people spoke badly about him. God told him to go back to his homeland and He would be with him.

ideas.children_he: יַעֲקֹב סִפֵּר לְנָשָׁיו עַל הַקְּשָׁיִים שֶׁעָבַר בָּעֲבוֹדָה.
ideas.children_en: Jacob talked with Rachel and Leah about problems with Laban. Laban tricked him, but God helped Jacob and gave him spotted sheep.

ideas.children_he: יַעֲקֹב הֶאֱמִין שֶׁהוּא לֹא לְבַד בְּדַרְכּוֹ.
ideas.children_en: Jacob had a dream about special colored sheep. God sent this to help him. Now it's time to leave and keep the promise to Bet El.

ideas.children_he: רָחֵל וְלֵאָה הִסְכִּימוּ לָצֵאת לַדֶּרֶךְ עִם מִשְׁפַּחְתָּן.
ideas.children_en: Rachel and Leah said they have no share at their father's house. They agree to go with Jacob because what he has is theirs.

ideas.children_he: יַעֲקֹב עָזַב בַּסֵּתֶר, וְרָחֵל לָקְחָה חֲפָצִים שֶׁל אָבִיהָ.
ideas.children_en: Laban left to shear his sheep, and Rachel stole her father's idols. Jacob left with his family and all his things without Laban knowing.

ideas.children_he: לָבָן רָדַף אַחֲרֵי יַעֲקֹב, וְהַמְּרִיבָה כִּמְעַט הֶחְמִירָה.
ideas.children_en: Laban chased Jacob with his family for seven days. God told him in a dream not to speak badly to Jacob.

ideas.children_he: לָבָן הִרְגִּישׁ שֶׁהִסְתִּירוּ מִמֶּנּוּ אֶת הַפְּרֵדָה.
ideas.children_en: Laban met Jacob and accused him of running away and stealing daughters. But he did not hurt him because God warned him.

ideas.children_he: יַעֲקֹב פָּחַד שֶׁיִּקְחוּ מִמֶּנּוּ אֶת מִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ.
ideas.children_en: Jacob was careful because he feared Laban might take his daughters. Laban looked for the idols Rachel stole but did not find them.

ideas.children_he: יַעֲקֹב סִפֵּר עַל שָׁנִים רַבּוֹת שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה קָשָׁה.
ideas.children_en: Jacob was angry because Laban chased him without reason. He told about his hard work for twenty years under Laban.

ideas.children_he: גַּם אַחֲרֵי מְרִיבָה אֲרֻכָּה אֶפְשָׁר לְחַפֵּשׂ הֶסְכֵּם.
ideas.children_en: Laban does not accept Jacob's claims. He says all property is his, and suggests making a covenant between them for the future.

ideas.children_he: הָאֲבָנִים הָיוּ סִימָן לַהַבְטָחָה בֵּין שְׁנֵי הַצְּדָדִים.
ideas.children_en: Jacob raised a stone and made a heap of stones called Galed, to remember the covenant and keep peace between them.

ideas.children_he: כְּשֶׁנִּפְרָדִים, חָשׁוּב לְהַבְטִיחַ לֹא לִפְגֹּעַ זֶה בָּזֶה.
ideas.children_en: The place is called the Watchtower and God will protect the agreement. Laban promises not to harm Jacob's family, and God is the witness.

ideas.children_he: הַהֶסְכֵּם קָבַע גְּבוּלוֹת כְּדֵי לִמְנֹעַ מְרִיבָה חֲדָשָׁה.
ideas.children_en: Laban points to the heap and stone as signs of their agreement so they will not harm each other in the future.

ideas.children_he: שְׁנֵי הַצְּדָדִים הִבְטִיחוּ לְכַבֵּד אֶת הַהֶסְכֵּם.
ideas.children_en: Laban says God of their fathers will judge between them, and Jacob promises to keep the covenant by the God of Isaac.

ideas.children_he: אֲרוּחָה מְשֻׁתֶּפֶת סִיְּמָה אֶת הַמְּרִיבָה בְּשָׁלוֹם.
ideas.children_en: Jacob offered a sacrifice and invited everyone to eat on the mountain to celebrate their new covenant.
